intent.title: Keep Build evidence out of oversized commits

evidence.locator: The public fake lifecycle retains an uncited required artifact larger than 5 MiB and asserts runtime paths are absent from the committed tree.
`build_summary/4` emits an allowlisted summary and `write_complete_package/5` keeps the full record at its runtime locator.

scenarios.reason: The implementation publishes compact summary/navigation while retaining the bound full record outside Git; recorded Stop verification passed for this Candidate.

evidence.locator: The lifecycle assertions preserve distinct role snapshots, failed attempts, finding history, semantic cited evidence, and uncited binary target evidence in the runtime record.
`matching_identity/3` binds Intent, Build, accepted Candidate, Developer session, and ordered attempt identities to the decoded record.

scenarios.reason: Full tracking evidence remains authoritative and bound to compact results without conflating role citations or retention with semantic review.

evidence.locator: `validate_staged_publication/0` measures staged Git blob sizes, applies both fixed limits, excludes deletions, and reports aggregate largest contributors.
Covers exact equality, aggregate one-byte overage, per-file one-byte overage, and runtime-path rejection.

scenarios.reason: Final publication validates actual staged blobs with the specified boundaries and actionable diagnostics; Approved-input preflight also covers aggregate-only impossibility.

evidence.locator: Final publication invokes staged-tree identity assertion and staged publication validation immediately before commit.
NUL-delimited unusual runtime filename control verifies force-staged ignored runtime evidence is rejected.

scenarios.reason: The final-tree guard covers all staged destinations, including force-staged runtime paths and newline-containing names, before commit.

evidence.locator: Preflight occurs before branch/provider lifecycle work and names oversized files, aggregate total, and largest contributors.
Aggregate-only Approved-package overage preserves approval/index state and proves the harness was not invoked.

scenarios.reason: Known impossible Approved inputs fail before provider launch; publication code retains existing rollback and immutable-input checks for later failure paths.

evidence.locator: Both connected live routes copy bound tracking archives, delete fixtures, then call `audit_retained!/1`.
Retained compact-summary regression resolves the copied archive after fixture removal.
Stop's recorded `check` and `live` receipts both passed for this exact Candidate.

scenarios.reason: Live consumers retain and independently resolve digest-bound archive copies after cleanup, while the passed declared live receipt confirms the affected route settled.

evidence.locator: Resolver rejects absent, byte-mismatched, unsupported, and identity-mismatched summaries/records and accepts only the exact bound record.
Focused controls cover missing archive, corruption, summary-version, Intent, Candidate, Build, and Developer-session mismatches.
Documents concise clone results and explicit unavailability of cleaned local archives.

scenarios.reason: Compact evidence remains separately readable, while full inspection is bound to an available, digest-valid, identity-valid archive and rejects corrupt substitutes.

evidence.locator: The retained summaries rewrite the archive locator only in the log copy; the audit invocation still receives the disposable fixture before `File.rm_rf!(fixture)`.
`resolve_tracking!/1` resolves the summary archive at audit time, but this consumer is not invoked on the retained summary after fixture cleanup.

origin.reason: The live consumer does not verify retained summary/archive copies after the fixture is removed. It audits the original fixture before cleanup, leaving the required post-cleanup resolvability and digest-validity behavior unexercised.

evidence.locator: `preserve_tracking/3` copies archives, rewrites retained summary locators, and both live routes invoke `audit_retained!/1` after fixture removal.
Post-cleanup retained-summary regression test resolves the copied archive.

current_disposition.reason: Closed: the retained-copy audit now runs after disposable fixture cleanup and resolves the copied archive.

evidence.locator: `matching_identity/2` compares only `summary.intent.id` to `record.intent.id`; it does not bind summary candidate, Build, or session identity fields to the resolved record.
The only wrong-identity control alters the Intent ID; it does not cover an altered accepted Candidate or Build/session binding in a digest-valid summary.

origin.reason: The compact-summary resolver accepts a digest-valid archive even if summary identity fields such as `candidate_id` are altered. This does not meet the required accepted-Candidate and valid identity bindings or the full wrong-identity corruption control.

evidence.locator: `matching_identity/3` validates Intent, Build, accepted Candidate, Developer session, and ordered attempt identities against the decoded record.
Controls reject changed Candidate, Build, and Developer-session summary identities.

current_disposition.reason: Closed: resolver identity validation now binds the material summary identities to the exact decoded record.

evidence.locator: `preflight_approved_budget/1` reports an empty over-file list and aggregate total only when many individually valid Approved files exceed the aggregate limit; it does not name largest contributors.
Existing budget test combines aggregate excess with a per-file excess and has no control for many individually valid files exceeding the aggregate limit.

origin.reason: Preflight aggregate-limit failures do not identify largest contributing paths and byte counts, despite the contract requiring enough contributors to explain an aggregate failure. Add the required individually-valid aggregate-overage control and actionable preflight diagnostics.

evidence.locator: `preflight_approved_budget/1` sorts and reports up to eight largest path/byte contributors on aggregate failure.
`approved_aggregate_oversize` uses three individually-valid 4,000,000-byte files and asserts diagnostics plus no harness invocation.

current_disposition.reason: Closed: aggregate-only Approved-package overage now produces actionable largest-contributor diagnostics and is covered before provider launch.
